newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: IDB plans $330 million in 1997 loans to Guatemala.
newsitem.headline: IDB plans $330 million in 1997 loans to Guatemala.

text.p: The Interamerican Development Bank (IDB) said on Thursday it planned to lend Guatemala $330 million this year for programs linked to the peace process in this Central American nation.

"We are here now to begin fulfilling the commitments we took on as a bank. The bank is programming ... for 1997 on the order of $330 million" in loans for Guatemala, IDB president Enrique Iglesias told reporters at a news conference.
Iglesias said the funds would go to projects including infrastructure, housing, education, judicial reform, financial reform, and small business programs.
Guatemala ended 36 years of civil war December 29 with a historic peace treaty between the government and leftist rebels.

The promised loans from the IDB are part of a $1.9 billion international aid package promised in January by different countries and multilateral lending institutions for programs to support the Guatemalan peace process.
In 1996 the bank loaned Guatemala $150 million, and is planning about $200 million a year during four years of peace projects, Iglesias said.
Guatemala, which has one of the lowest tax burdens in the Americas, has promised to improve tax collection to make its own contribution to peace programs.
